skill.name: angular
skill.description: Guide for modern Angular v20+ development, including Signals, Standalone Components, zoneless change detection, SSR, hydration, routing, dependency injection, forms, testing, and performance patterns.
skill.summary: Build modern Angular v20+ applications with Signals, standalone components, SSR, hydration, and performance-focused patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 102 static findings were adjudicated as false positives after source review. The flagged patterns are Angular documentation links, Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, relative lazy-loading imports, or Angular APIs rather than executable malicious behavior.

remediation.issue: Scanner noise from Markdown backticks and code fences
remediation.suggestion: Use clearer fenced examples or scanner suppression metadata so documentation formatting is not mistaken for shell execution.

remediation.issue: Example network calls and placeholder URLs trigger network detections
remediation.suggestion: Label sample endpoints as non-executable examples and keep external links limited to trusted documentation references.

remediation.issue: Angular API names were misclassified as filesystem or reconnaissance behavior
remediation.suggestion: Add brief comments around Angular Signals and resolver examples to clarify that they are framework APIs.

static_findings.snippet: | `on idle`        | Low-priority, hydrate when browser idle |
| `on viewport`    | Hydrate when element enters viewport    |
| `on interaction` | Hydrate on first user interaction       |
| Signal not updating UI         | Ensure `OnPush` + call signal as function `count()` |

content.value_statement: Modern Angular changes quickly across Signals, standalone components, zoneless apps, and hydration. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through current Angular patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Angular Signals, computed values, effects, and signal-based inputs.
Shows standalone component setup, routing, lazy loading, guards, and resolvers.
Covers zoneless change detection, OnPush usage, and performance patterns.
Guides SSR, hydration, incremental hydration, and TransferState decisions.
Provides Angular testing patterns for signal components and signal inputs.
limitations: It does not inspect a project unless the user provides files or context.
It cannot verify runtime behavior without build, test, or browser execution.
It focuses on modern Angular and is not for AngularJS migrations.
Some future-version guidance may need confirmation against current Angular releases.

use_cases.title: Design a New Angular Feature
use_cases.description: Plan components, routes, state, and data loading using current Angular architecture.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing Angular App
use_cases.description: Replace older module, input, or change detection patterns with safer incremental updates.

use_cases.title: Review Angular Performance Choices
use_cases.description: Evaluate Signals, defer blocks, hydration, and lazy loading choices before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new Angular component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Angular skill to design a standalone component for this feature. Include inputs, outputs, state, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Signal State
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for reactive component state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Angular skill to convert this component state to Signals. Explain computed values, effects, and any RxJS boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for routing and data loading.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Angular skill to refactor these routes with lazy loading, functional guards, and resolvers. Identify migration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit SSR and Hydration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review for rendering strategy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Angular skill to review this SSR and hydration plan. Cover defer blocks, TransferState, fetch behavior, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Plan a modern Angular dashboard with lazy routes and local state.
output_examples.output: A structured implementation plan covering standalone components, route-level loading, Signals for local state, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Review a component that mixes RxJS streams and Signals.
output_examples.output: A clear recommendation showing which state should stay in RxJS, which state should become Signals, and why.

output_examples.input: Prepare an SSR migration checklist for an Angular storefront.
output_examples.output: A practical checklist for hydration, TransferState, data loading, image optimization, and regression testing.

best_practices: Provide the Angular version, project structure, and constraints before asking for architecture changes.
Ask for incremental migration steps when updating established Angular applications.
Run build, tests, and browser checks after applying generated Angular changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for AngularJS migration plans without a dedicated migration workflow.
Do not apply zoneless or SSR changes broadly without project-specific testing.
Do not copy future-version examples without checking the installed Angular version.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets modern Angular v20+ patterns, with notes about later Angular features.

faq.question: Can it help with Signals?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers writable signals, computed values, effects, signal inputs, and Signal-based state patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace Angular documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes common patterns, but current Angular documentation remains the authority.

faq.question: Can it migrate NgModule applications?
faq.answer: It can suggest incremental standalone migration steps for Angular apps, but not AngularJS migration.

faq.question: Does it run Angular commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent must decide which commands to run.

faq.question: Can it review SSR and hydration designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SSR setup, hydration triggers, TransferState considerations, and testing guidance.
